name: Primer to Candy Paint
why_it_works: A dull, beat-up starting point makes people root for the car. Showing the ugly middle stages proves the work is real and earns the right to the big finish, so the final shine feels deserved instead of staged.

hook.pattern: Open on the worst angle of the car and state how long it took to fix.
examples: This {{vehicle}} came in rusted. {{hours}} hours later, watch.
Nobody wanted this {{vehicle}}. Stay for the last shot.
Primer, tape, and {{hours}} hours. Here's the payoff.

variables.name: vehicle
variables.description: Year and model, or a plain description

variables.name: hours

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of a faded, rust-spotted {{vehicle}} in a garage bay, flat fluorescent light, low three-quarter angle, dust in the air

beats.voiceover: First we took it back to bare metal.

visual.prompt: Close-up of a sanding disc moving across a car panel, sparks and dust, harsh work light, handheld vertical 9:16

beats.voiceover: Then primer. This is the part nobody posts.

visual.prompt: The {{vehicle}} in grey primer with masking tape lines, garage bay, cool overhead light, wide vertical 9:16
Painter in a respirator spraying a glossy color layer inside a paint booth, mist catching the light, side angle, vertical 9:16
The finished {{vehicle}} in {{finish}} rolling out of a dark garage into golden-hour light, slow low tracking shot, reflections sliding across the paint, vertical 9:16

cta: Book your {{offer}} at {{shop_name}}; link in bio.

craft.notes: Spend the middle on the unglamorous stages (bare metal, primer, tape) so the viewer feels the labor. Keep the reveal silent with only the engine or music; talking over the money shot weakens it.

do_not: Use another shop's car or a stock photo as the 'before'
Show license plates or VINs of a customer car without permission
Skip the middle and jump straight from rust to shine; it looks fake
Spend the clip_hero credits before the client approves the still of the final car
